answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/import-subscriptions, the 2026-11-07 capture guides API migration from a third-party, in-house system, or existing Stripe account into Stripe Billing: prepare customers and prices, map source customer and price IDs, align schedule start and billing anchors with remaining terms, and test in a sandbox (new lines 9-16, 63-83, 102-115). For customers to be charged automatically, it requires a default payment source; without one, subscription invoices cannot collect (new 16, 45-61). Third-party PAN import must precede setting defaults, but the processor-import prerequisite is unnecessary for Stripe-to-Stripe migration (new 15, 59-61). Both captures permit Subscription API creation and recommend Schedules for future starts (new 113; old 111). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-migration-api]] now states these boundaries; the final list-Subscriptions call checks object existence only (new 128-138), not completed billing, payment, or reconciliation.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/overview, the 2026-11-07 capture describes subscription creation, invoices, payments, status transitions, recovery and active entitlements. Its first-invoice 23-hour `incomplete` rule is scoped to `charge_automatically` (new 31-43); `send_invoice` without a trial can begin `active` before the first invoice is paid (new 33). It distinguishes eight status labels and makes reactivation from `past_due` or `unpaid` depend on a most-recent or all-applicable-invoices setting; an applicable invoice is finalized, due and unsettled within a 37-month lookback (new 75-108). An initial `incomplete` payment needs integration collection because Smart Retries do not retry it, while recurring failures can use configured retry rules (new 151-164). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-overview]] retains these conditions, permits product access during `trialing` (new 77), and gates paid initial-payment recovery on active subscription or active entitlements (new 49,154,180), rather than a webhook name alone.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/overview, the substantive changes from the 2026-05-12 capture are the collection-method split (new 31-43 versus old 40-55), configurable invoice-based status resolution and conditional active outcome (new 77-108,118 versus old 103-120), initial-versus-recurring retry separation (new 151-164 versus old 149-155), and active entitlements tied to activation rather than mere creation while `trialing` still permits product access (new 49,77 versus old 59,103). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-overview]] preserves the May payment_behavior options and first-invoice editing constraints as dated evidence (old 29-38,71-77); omission in November is no proof of deprecation. The newer authentication example uses `stripe.handleNextAction` (new 179) versus older `stripe.ConfirmCardPayment` (old 173), without proving SDK-wide removal. A delayed method can be `active` while PaymentIntent is `processing` and can remain active after a later failure and invoice void (new 124,137); neither `active` nor `invoice.paid` alone proves every invoice or delayed payment finally settled.
